interest: Lawyer A. L. Wirin's fight for a passport to defend Nisei citizenship claims, 1949.
overview: This file documents efforts in late 1949 by prominent civil liberties attorney A. L. Wirin and Washington counsel Charles A. Horsky (of Covington, Burling, Rublee, O'Brian & Shorb) to overturn the State Department's denial of a passport to Wirin. Wirin represented multiple Japanese Americans (Nisei) residing in Japan who were alleged by the U.S. government to have forfeited their American citizenship due to their actions or presence in Japan before or during World War II. After the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California ordered depositions of several plaintiffs and a witness to be taken before the U.S. Consul in Yokohama, Wirin sought to travel to Japan to attend the proceedings, but his passport application was denied because General Douglas MacArthur's SCAP headquarters did not desire his presence. Following petitions asserting a violation of due process sent to Secretary of State Dean Acheson and Legal Adviser Adrian S. Fisher, the State Department agreed to give Wirin's application further consideration.

subfiles.about: Charles A. Horsky writes to State Department Legal Adviser Adrian S. Fisher requesting intervention regarding the denial of a passport to attorney A. L. Wirin to take depositions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Charles A. Horsky asks Legal Adviser Fisher to help A. L. Wirin, denied a passport to take court-ordered depositions in Japan for Nisei citizenship suits.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles A. Horsky to Adrian S. Fisher regarding A. L. Wirin's passport denial

subfiles.about: A. L. Wirin appeals directly to Secretary of State Dean Acheson to reconsider the denial of his passport to travel to Japan to represent Japanese American clients in court-ordered depositions.
subfiles.summary: A. L. Wirin appeals to Acheson against his passport denial, made because SCAP did not want him in Japan, saying he was denied due process.
subfiles.title: Copy of letter from A. L. Wirin to Secretary of State Dean Acheson appealing passport denial

subfiles.about: Federal District Judge Paul J. McCormick orders that depositions of seven Nisei plaintiffs and one witness be taken before the U.S. Consul in Yokohama, Japan.
subfiles.summary: Judge Paul J. McCormick orders depositions of seven Japanese American plaintiffs and a witness before the U.S. Consul at Yokohama in suits against Acheson over citizenship.
subfiles.title: Order Directing Taking of Depositions in U.S. District Court (Southern District of California)
subfiles.to: Parties and Counsel of Record, U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California

subfiles.about: State Department Legal Adviser Adrian S. Fisher informs Charles A. Horsky that A. L. Wirin's passport application is receiving serious consideration.
subfiles.summary: Fisher tells Horsky that Wirin's passport application will receive further consideration.
subfiles.title: Letter from Adrian S. Fisher to Charles A. Horsky regarding A. L. Wirin's passport application
